acceptance_criteria: a tenant admin can submit a new brand_colors.primary value through the screen, it round-trips through REQ-382's endpoint, and a confirmation is shown, matching EO-001's positive half

a regression test confirms StatusBadge's approved/waiting/failed colours are unchanged after a tenant colour change -- matching EO-002
the screen's own form has no field/control/code path capable of submitting a key this requirement did not itself add -- stated and verified explicitly

result.summary:
Read lib/letflow/design/req383-appearance-settings-screen.md in full, independently. AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4/AC5 each map to a concrete, unambiguous design element (§2-3 for AC1, §0/§3.4/§4 for AC2, §6 for AC3, §5 for AC4, §7/§8 for AC5) -- no TBD/deferral language found; the four recorded open questions (OQ-1..OQ-4) are legitimate non-blocking implementation-detail flags (nav-link placement, queryKeys timing, e2e isolation mechanism, DOM-read-vs-cache justification), not silent resolutions of anything an acceptance criterion depends on. Cross-module dependencies (§10) are complete and accurate against the files actually read. Independently re-verified the design's single highest-risk claim against the REAL merged code: read lib/letflow/routers/tenant_settings.ex (handle_patch/patch_tenant_settings -- 200 success via Response.ok(conn, settings_response_map(tenant, updated_tenant)) = {tenant_id, settings}; 422 via Response.unprocessable(conn, changeset_error_message(changeset))), lib/letflow/api/error.ex (Error.unprocessable/1 builds %{type, title: "Unprocessable Entity", status: 422, detail: detail, trace_id}, @derive Jason.Encoder only:[:type,:title,:status,:detail,:trace_id]), and web/src/api/client.ts's request/1 (client.ts ~127-145: on a non-ok/401/429/409 status, message = body['title'] ?? body['message'] ?? statusText -- resolves to the literal string 'Unprocessable Entity' since body has a 'title' key; details = body itself since Object.keys(body).length>0, i.e. the full decoded problem-details object including its own 'detail' key). This confirms the design's claim precisely: err.message on a 422 is the generic 'Unprocessable Entity' title, and the real plain-language WCAG message is reachable ONLY via err.details.detail. No discrepancy found -- this premise is correct.

FAILING the gate on check 2e (no implementation code present), which is a hard, no-partial-credit failure per WF-02 Step 1b and the task's explicit framing ('no actual .ts/.tsx code bodies, only signatures/types/shapes'). Two design sections contain real, complete, copy-paste-ready TypeScript implementation code, not signatures or type shapes: (1) design doc lines 234-240 (§3.3) -- the `tenantSettingsApi` object is a fully implemented module export with a working arrow-function body (`client.patch<TenantSettingsPatchResponse>('/api/v1/tenant/settings', { settings: { brand_colors: { primary } } } satisfies TenantSettingsPatchBody)`), not a signature -- a correct signature would state `patchBrandColorPrimary(primary: string): Promise<TenantSettingsPatchResponse>` and describe the call shape in prose/type terms, not emit the literal working call. (2) design doc lines 258-285 (§3.4) -- the `useMutation({...})` block is a complete, real onSuccess/onError implementation with actual control flow (a ternary on `apiErr.details?.detail`, sequenced state-setter calls, a toast call) -- this is an implementation, not a shape description. Both blocks are fenced as literal ```/```typescript code, not comments describing intended behaviour (contrast with §3.1's readCurrentAppliedPrimary, which correctly keeps its body as a `//`-commented algorithm description under a `@spec`-style signature -- that section passes; §3.3 and §3.4 do not follow that pattern and cross into real code).
